docs.title: Welcome to The Lab
docs.text:
The Lab is a semi-serious roleplay city. We want real, immersive stories, but we're not here to ruin your night over a slip of the tongue. You won't get banned for accidentally breaking character or saying something OOC once or twice while you find your feet.

What we ask in return is simple: take the RP seriously, and value your character's life. Play like your character is a real person: someone who wants to survive, reacts to danger, and lives with the consequences of their choices. That one mindset prevents most problems before a rule ever has to be quoted.

The one-line version: Be immersive, value your life, and treat people well OOC. Get those three right and you'll rarely think about the rulebook at all.

docs.title: How to read this book
docs.text:
• Everyone should read How We Handle Rules and The Golden Rules.
  • Know the lines that have no second chances: Zero Tolerance.
  • The rest, like combat, death, and metagaming, is detail you can reference when a situation comes up.

We would rather coach a new player into a great community member than ban them. The rules exist to protect everyone from the small number of people who show up to cheat, grief, or hurt others, not to punish people for learning.

docs.title: Ban Guidelines
docs.text: We believe in being upfront about consequences. This page lays out how punishments generally work, so there are no surprises. These are guidelines, and staff always weigh context and intent, but this is the framework we work from.

docs.title: How escalation normally works
docs.text:
For ordinary RP mistakes (bad initiation, breaking character, minor NLR/meta slips), we escalate rather than jump straight to bans:

  1. Verbal / coaching: a heads-up, often in the moment. No formal mark.
  2. Formal warning: logged. You know it's on record.
  3. Kick: a reset for disruptive-but-not-malicious behavior.
  4. Temporary ban: for repeated issues or a more serious single incident.
  5. Permanent ban: for continued disregard after the above, or a severe violation.

A first honest mistake almost never lands past step 1 or 2. Where you land depends on intent and pattern, not just the act.

docs.title: Rough guide by violation
docs.text: Violation Typical first response Repeat / severe Minor RP mistakes (OOC slip, small NLR/meta) Verbal or warning Warning to temp ban RDM / VDM Warning to temp ban Temp to permanent Fail RP / not valuing life Warning Temp ban Combat logging Temp ban Permanent Powergaming / metagaming (deliberate) Warning to temp ban Permanent Exploiting bugs / duping Permanent ban N/A Cheating (mods, menus, injectors) Permanent ban (first offense) N/A Harassment / OOC toxicity toward a real person Permanent ban (first offense) N/A ERP (any form, public or private) Permanent ban (first offense) N/A Sexual content involving minors Permanent ban + reported N/A

docs.title: Permanent bans & returning
docs.text: Some permanent bans are eligible for a return through our official process (where offered, via review). Others, particularly cheating, harassment, ERP, and anything involving minors, may be final and non-negotiable. Every case is reviewed individually.

docs.title: What we consider
docs.text:
• Intent: honest mistake, or deliberate?
  • Pattern: first time, or the same thing again?
  • Impact: did it ruin the scene or the night for others?
  • Attitude: owning it vs. arguing in bad faith.
  • Honesty: lying to staff during a review makes everything worse.

docs.title: Appeals
docs.text:
Every ban can be appealed through the official appeal process, not by DMing staff. Appeal calmly, honestly, and with any evidence you have. A good-faith appeal is taken seriously; a hostile or dishonest one rarely goes anywhere.

Our promise: we'd rather coach a new player into a great community member than ban them. Bans exist to protect everyone else from the few people who are here to cheat, grief, or hurt others, not to punish people for learning.

docs.title: Combat: RDM, VDM & Initiation
docs.text: Combat is fine. Combat without roleplay is not. Every fight should come from a story, not appear out of nowhere.

docs.title: Initiation
docs.text:
Before you can shoot, rob, or attack someone, there must be initiation, a clear in-character interaction that gives them a real chance to respond. A demand, a threat, a reason. "I felt like it" is not initiation.

  • Give people a genuine moment to comply or react. Don't demand hands up and open fire in the same second.
  • Initiating on a whole group means the group can respond, but uninvolved bystanders are not automatically targets.

docs.title: RDM (Random Deathmatch)
docs.text: Killing or attacking someone without valid initiation or an RP reason is RDM. Don't do it. A shared story, a prior conflict, an active robbery. Those are reasons. Boredom is not.

docs.title: VDM (Vehicle Deathmatch)
docs.text: Using your vehicle as a weapon without RP, running people over or ramming for no reason, is VDM. Your car is a car, not a missile.

docs.title: Combat logging
docs.text:
Logging out during or right after an active RP scene (a fight, chase, robbery, or being detained) to escape it is prohibited. If you actually crash, get back as soon as you can and let people know what happened.

Quick test before you pull the trigger: Would this make sense in a story someone else is also enjoying? If yes, go. If it only makes sense as "I wanted the kill," stop.

docs.title: Death & the New Life Rule (NLR)
docs.text: How death works, and what your character is allowed to remember.

docs.title: The New Life Rule
docs.text:
When your character is downed and respawns (a "new life"), they do not remember the events that led to their death: not who killed them, why, or the details of that situation. That memory is gone.

  • Don't return to the scene of your death while it's still active.
  • Don't seek revenge on the people involved, based on knowledge your character shouldn't have.
  • Don't rejoin the fight you just died in.

docs.title: If you're revived instead of respawning
docs.text: If EMS or a player revives you, with no respawn and no new life, NLR generally does not wipe your memory. You were brought back, not reborn. Follow medical RP and any injuries or amnesia your revive scene establishes.

docs.title: Permadeath / character kills
docs.text:
Your character is not permanently dead from an ordinary downing. A true character kill only happens by agreement or through specific approved RP. It is not something one side can force in a random shootout.

The point of NLR: death should carry weight and let a scene end. Using post-death knowledge to grief the people who beat you drains all the tension out of the city. Take the L, start the next story.

docs.title: ERP & Content Boundaries
docs.text: The Lab does not permit erotic roleplay (ERP) of any kind. This is a full, no-exceptions policy. There is no "private," "consensual," or "fade to black" version that is allowed here. Keep sexual content out of the city entirely.

docs.title: What this means
docs.text:
• No sexual or erotic roleplay, in public or private, spoken, typed, or emoted.
  • No sexual content in RP, in-city channels, or anywhere the server touches.
  • Romance in RP is fine as a story. The moment it turns sexual, it stops.

docs.title: Why it's absolute
docs.text: We'd rather have one clear line everyone understands than a gray zone people "accidentally" wander into. There is nothing to interpret and nothing to negotiate: don't bring sexual content into The Lab.

docs.title: The hardest line of all
docs.text:
Any sexual content involving minors or characters depicted as minors, real or fictional, in any form, results in an immediate permanent ban and a report to the appropriate authorities. There is no roleplay justification, ever. "It's just a character" is not a defense.

ERP is a permanent-ban offense. See Zero Tolerance for enforcement.

docs.title: The Golden Rules
docs.text: These are the core expectations. Everything else in this book is detail.

docs.title: 1. Value your life (this one is enforced)
docs.text:
Your character wants to live. When a gun is in your face, when you're outnumbered, when a situation is truly dangerous, act like it. Comply, negotiate, be scared, look for a real way out. Don't do things a real person facing death would never do just because "it's a game."

Fear RP is not optional. Ignoring a credible threat to your life (pulling a weapon while surrounded and at gunpoint, or mouthing off to armed robbers with no plan) is one of the few RP rules we enforce firmly, because it wrecks the scene for everyone involved.

docs.title: 2. Keep IC and OOC separate
docs.text: In-character conflict stays in-character. Don't carry story grudges into OOC, and don't let OOC feelings bleed into your RP. A quick OOC slip in city is no big deal. Living your OOC drama through your character is.

docs.title: 3. Roleplay in good faith
docs.text: Give others a scene worth being in. Don't grief, don't ruin RP for the sake of "winning," and don't treat other players as NPCs. Everyone here is a person trying to tell a story, including you.

docs.title: 4. Respect people OOC, always
docs.text: You can be a villain in the city and a decent person out of it. Treat other players and staff with basic respect at all times. (See Zero Tolerance. This one has teeth.)

docs.title: How We Handle Rules
docs.text: We don't run this city with a stopwatch and a ban hammer. Context and intent matter. Most rule-breaks are honest mistakes, and we treat them that way.

docs.title: Most situations
docs.text:
For ordinary RP mistakes like a bad initiation, breaking character, or a messy scene, staff lean toward coaching and warnings first, and only escalate if it keeps happening or was clearly deliberate. A first honest mistake is a conversation, not a punishment.

Repeatedly "forgetting" the same rule stops looking like a mistake. Patterns escalate faster than one-offs.

docs.title: Some things are different
docs.text:
A short list of violations skips the warning ladder entirely, because they attack the integrity of the server or the safety of our players. These are permanent, first-offense bans, with no warnings:

  • Cheating / exploiting
  • Harassment / OOC toxicity toward a real person
  • ERP (erotic roleplay) of any kind
  • Anything sexual involving minors

See Zero Tolerance for the full list, and Ban Guidelines for exactly how everything else escalates.

docs.title: The spirit of it
docs.text: If you're playing in good faith, you have a lot of room. If you're here to cheat, grief, or hurt people, you don't. Staff decisions are made case-by-case with that spirit in mind. The goal is a healthy city, not a body count.

docs.title: Metagaming & Powergaming
docs.text: Two of the most common ways good RP gets quietly ruined. Know the difference between them.

docs.title: Metagaming
docs.text:
Using information your character didn't learn in-character to affect your RP. If you know it from a stream, a Discord message, a DM, or from spectating, your character does not know it.

  • Acting on something you saw on someone's stream ("stream sniping").
  • Using OOC info (Discord, DMs, party chat) to find or act against someone in city.
  • Knowing a stranger's name, job, or history your character was never actually told.

Your character only knows what they have seen and heard in the city. That's it.

docs.title: Powergaming
docs.text:
Forcing outcomes, or giving your character abilities and knowledge they realistically shouldn't have, which removes other players' ability to respond.

  • Forcing actions on someone without giving them a chance to react (/me knocks you out and ties you up with no opening for them to respond).
  • Doing things your character couldn't realistically do, like surviving impossible injuries, having skills you never established, or fixing a car with a snap of your fingers.
  • Using RP commands to narrate reality onto another player instead of attempting an action they can react to.

docs.title: The fix for both
docs.text: Roleplay attempts, not results. Give people room to respond. Keep OOC knowledge out of IC decisions. When in doubt, ask: does the other person still get a say in what happens? If the answer is no, you're probably powergaming.

docs.title: If something goes wrong in-city
docs.text:
• Use the in-game report system to reach staff. It's the fastest, most trackable way.
  • Don't break your current RP to argue OOC. Finish the scene, then report; staff can review what happened.
  • Gather what you can: who (names / IDs), when, and what happened. Clips help enormously.

docs.title: Report in good faith
docs.text: Reports are for genuine rule-breaks, not for losing a fight. Filing false or spam reports to harass someone is itself a violation.

docs.title: Staff conduct
docs.text: Our staff are held to a higher standard, not a looser one. They enforce with context and fairness, coach before they punish (outside the zero-tolerance list), and don't play favorites. If you feel a decision was wrong, there's a calm, proper channel to appeal it. Use it, rather than taking it to public drama.

docs.title: Appeals
docs.text: Ban appeals and unban requests go through the official process only. Don't DM staff to appeal. It won't be handled there, and it may hurt your case.

docs.title: Zero Tolerance
docs.text: Almost everything in this city gets a warning and a conversation. These do not. The following are permanent, first-offense bans, because they attack the server itself or the people in it.

docs.title: Cheating & exploiting → permanent ban
docs.text:
Any cheat software, injectors, mod menus, macros for unfair advantage, or deliberately exploiting bugs (duping money/items, out-of-map abuse, etc.).

  • First offense: permanent ban. No warnings.
  • Being caught with cheat software installed counts, whether or not you "used it here."

docs.title: Harassment → permanent ban
docs.text:
Real-world targeted harassment, hate speech, threats, sexual harassment, predatory behavior, doxxing, or using the server to hurt someone as a person.

  • First offense: permanent ban. No warnings.
  • Villainy in-character is welcome. Attacking a real person OOC is not, and there is no IC excuse for it.

docs.title: ERP (Erotic Roleplay) → permanent ban
docs.text:
The Lab does not allow erotic roleplay in any form, whether public or private, consensual or not. There is no permitted version of it here.

  • First offense: permanent ban. No warnings.
  • Romance as story is fine; sexual content is not. See ERP & Content Boundaries.

docs.title: Anything sexual involving minors → permanent ban + reported
docs.text:
Any sexual content involving minors or characters depicted as minors, real or fictional, in any form.

  • Zero tolerance. Permanent ban, and reported to the appropriate authorities.
  • There is no roleplay justification, ever. "It's just a character" is not a defense.

docs.title: Returning after a permanent ban
docs.text:
Some permanent bans are eligible for return through our official process only, never DMs or side deals. Cheating, harassment, ERP, and anything involving minors are reviewed individually, and some are simply final, with no return.

There is no "I didn't know." These lines, cheating, exploiting, harassment, OOC toxicity, ERP, and anything sexual involving minors, are what keep the city safe and fair. Cross them and you're gone.
